questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should honk to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must happen only in areas where passing is legal and safe.

questions.question: The only way to remove alcohol from your body is through:
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. There is no faster way to sober up.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes in both the front and rear.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can:

options.text: Be safe if you stay under the speed limit.
Be safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
Be safe if no other vehicles are near you.
Cause you to slide into another lane or off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause you to slide into another lane or off the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may not be able to hold the turn and could slide into another lane or leave the road. Slow down for turns.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after drinking one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Alcohol effects may still be present.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. However, alcohol can still affect your ability to ride safely even after waiting.

questions.question: Before riding, check your tires for all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Check tire air pressure, tread, and general wear before each ride. Shininess is not important for safety.

questions.question: Which material offers the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcycle riders. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs completely.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should you position yourself in your lane?

options.text: Always on the left side of the lane.
Always on the right side of the lane.
Always in the center of the lane.
Wherever is safest for current conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever is safest for current conditions.
questions.explanation: Change your lane position based on road conditions and hazards. There is no single position that is always best.

questions.question: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you to:
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Bright-colored clothing makes you more visible to other drivers during day and night. Choose clothes that increase your visibility.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast can:

options.text: Cause you to drift into another lane.
Be safer than going too slowly.
Help you stay in your lane.
Be okay because motorcycles are small.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause you to drift into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before you turn.

questions.question: You should keep a safe distance behind other vehicles:

options.text: To give yourself time to see and react to problems ahead.
So you can follow closely behind other cars.
To help traffic counters count you as a vehicle.
To make other drivers cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give yourself time to see and react to problems ahead.
questions.explanation: Keeping a safe distance gives you enough space to stop or move out of the way if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. You can also see hazards on the road better, such as potholes.

questions.question: The best lane position is one that:

options.text: Lets you travel at the fastest speed.
Allows you to use the air draft from other vehicles.
Puts you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and allows them to see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears. Choose a position that gives you the most space.

questions.question: Before riding, you should check everything except:
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Riders should wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear bright clothing all the time.
Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.
Wear dark clothing all the time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing all the time.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright colors when riding so other drivers can see you, even during the day.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are all slippery for motorcycles. Dry pavement provides the best grip.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Not be worn during the day.

questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials to be more visible, especially at night. Bright clothing with reflective materials makes you easier for other drivers to see.

questions.question: Your body can eliminate about ______ of alcohol per hour.
questions.explanation: On average, the human body can eliminate about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Which colors make riders most visible?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be seen by other drivers.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: Which surface does NOT provide poor traction?
questions.explanation: Several surfaces have poor traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings are all more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should ride:

options.text: In any part of the lane.
In the part of the lane closest to the shoulder.
In the part of the lane where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the part of the lane where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in a position where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Usually this is the center of the lane. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position makes you more visible.

questions.question: Riding alongside a car:

options.text: Can place you in a blind spot.
Is not an issue unless the roadway is wet.
Can make driving easier for the other motorist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can place you in a blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in the driver's blind spot, and the vehicle blocks your escape route.

questions.question: If your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks, you will:

options.text: Experience a sudden increase in power to the rear wheel.
Experience a sudden loss of power to the rear wheel.
Experience a sudden loss of power to the front wheel.
Experience a sudden increase in power to the front wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experience a sudden loss of power to the rear wheel.
questions.explanation: If your drive chain or belt breaks, you will immediately lose power to the rear wheel.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards or conditions.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: Make it easier for others to see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make it easier for others to see you.
questions.explanation: A bright helmet protects you in a crash and helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: If a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Encourage them to ride on quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has drunk too much to ride. Take their keys if needed and arrange another way for them to get home.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle operator should be prepared for:

options.text: A car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
Other drivers to see you and stay out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
questions.explanation: Be ready for a parked car to suddenly pull into traffic. Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right to stay as far away as possible.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in broad daylight. To be more visible, you should:
questions.explanation: Since most crashes occur during the day, always wear bright clothing when riding, even in daylight.
